BLOCK — performance/298 at 12bdede47db345264785d667f50ced08ef85e8dc, base44f313e4; answers01a1fa15-962d-7312-b41c-4033d5ae5aa2. First C34 round. Keep holding until merge.

P298-001 — MEDIUM, blocking: new bounce holder acquisition is unbounded (justfile790-803, call796).
The new no-server fallback invokes synchronous lsof -U inside command substitution with no supervision. It is after the bounded tmux setter and its bounded post-SIGKILL wait, not inside either budget. A blocked lsof can hold the bounce indefinitely before the old daemon is signalled; PIJ_BOUNCE_UNSAFE is consulted only after it returns. This reintroduces an unbounded evidence read on the failure path whose prior helper was explicitly bounded in F242/F244.
Own scratch smoke: nice -n19 node /tmp/p298-bounce-bound-probe.mjs, exit0. It extracts the actual complete bounce-rs recipe from the exact review tree, fakes release/install/npm/tmux/lsof at the boundaries, and substitutes one owned sleep for the old daemon. The one holder lsof remained running at4501.839667ms after entry, and the owned old process remained alive. External supervisor then removed only its owned process group and scratch. This is a controlled blocked-helper observation, not a measured live-lsof duration. No Cargo build, production resource read or production daemon signal occurred. Runner and raw result: /tmp/p298-bounce-bound-probe.mjs, /tmp/p298-bounce-bound-receipt.json.
Required: supervise the new holder acquisition and its cleanup, fail closed on timeout/read failure without stopping the old daemon, and cover that behavior with an isolated bounded regression. Resolve the new lsof by absolute path with an explicit test seam; quoting and exact path semantics remain security/reviewer's domain. No expansion into unrelated older port-lsof calls is required for this finding.

Cost accounting:
- macOS sweep CLI calls Holders::read once. One /usr/sbin/lsof, one stdout-reader thread, nominal50 try_wait calls/s with in-process20ms sleeps for a configured10s (~500 checks), zero subprocess per poll. Once paths arrive it stats each path and builds HashSet(dev,ino). The scan still sorts directory names and performs metadata/set lookups/nonwaiting flock per candidate, zero per-entry launches. Cost scales with the user's processes/open descriptors, returned bound paths and directory size, not zero fleet scaling. Linux reads /proc/net/unix in-process, zero lsof launches.
- Fixture exited(pid): nominal100 in-process kill(pid,0) calls/s with10ms sleeps, configured2s (~200 intervals plus terminal check) per Drop. F concurrent dropping fixtures give approximately100F syscalls/s while waiting, never a subprocess per poll and never per live seat at rest. ESRCH alone proves exit; EPERM/reused PID is conservative. PrivateTmux obtains PID from its existing startup command, no extra launch. Four other fixture types add one synchronous tmux display-message at Drop, in addition to the pre-existing kill-server. Governance fixture already owns its foreground server child.
- Bounce: zero or one added lsof -U and one id -u, once per refusal-path bounce; no per-entry work or daemon recurrence. Existing tmux setter/postkill /bin/sleep0.1 cadence and daemon stop /bin/sleep0.2 cadence are unchanged. The new read has no deadline: P298-001.
- F246: no extra success-path launches; still two mktemp+two mv for running and finished publication. A failing mktemp adds one rm(stamp). A write/move failure after a temp exists can add two rm calls (temp and stamp), not universally one. Both publication attempts can fail in one batch. Failure to publish/remove running exits7 before cargo; existing EXIT trap releases the held lock. Sources can already have been touched and temp deletion may have failed, so this is not a claim of literally zero filesystem mutation. Failure to publish/remove finished leaves running and warns. No normal-path polling or retry was added.
- No production daemon loop, poll, timer, task or launch-site change. pane_observer changes are test-only; the new process_exists helper is used here by testkit. No new steady-state per-seat process work or spawn_sites.rs entry is required by this delta. No live fleet probe was duplicated for a zero daemon-runtime delta.

Boundaries and evidence quality:
The sweep's10s is a configured child-status-poll budget, not an absolute end-to-end ceiling. Command spawn and reader-thread creation precede the deadline; kill()+blocking wait() and successful reader.join() are outside it (tmux_sweep.rs270-300). A descendant holding stdout was not exercised; no claim that real /usr/sbin/lsof forks one. This is a source qualification, separate from the reproduced bounce blocker.
The fixture2s bounds the kill0 loop only, not the preceding server_pid().output(), existing kill-server().output(), filesystem work or scheduler/syscall latency. No whole-Drop2s claim is supported.
Read coder /tmp/f245-receipts.md and /tmp/f245-checks2.log. The latter is a retained all15-sensor pass envelope, not a rerun or independently HEAD-stamped per-test transcript. F246 RED/GREEN27/27 and MF1-MF7/MG1-MG3 are coder summary receipts. The PR's lsof~0.1s is explicitly an estimate; sweep657ms/52032 stale/172 bound files is retained coder summary only, with no raw dry-run output/exact command. Neither is promoted to an independent measurement. Reviewer's Darwin alias/full-backlog/parser/failclosed mutation results remain separate role evidence. This performance verdict does not release the global sweep APPLY hold.
Read bee's independent runtime.json at /Users/jordanknight/.copilot/session-state/ef9fda2b-0b8e-47cd-b114-9d1a602c4ad0/files/review298-probe/: server PID9470 confirmed by display-message,128 backlog clients then errno61, lsof still lists its bound /tmp path, and the canonical /private/tmp path matches the same dev/ino. Cleanup kill-server exit0. This supports the exercised kernel-holder evidence/alias handling, not lsof timeout behavior or complete failclosed mutation coverage, which remains reviewer's separate gate.
Product audit scoped independently to daemon/tmux/core/testkit refusal literals/call sites: daemon serve.rs ConnectionRefused is HTTP accept-error classification, not a server-absence policy. No other new production inference or launch found. Full product audit and destructive parse/path correctness are independent reviewer gates.

Destructive semantics:
Sweep policy = no holder for the candidate socket, with fixture prefix/type/ownership/lock predicates. Unknown must preserve files. The young-entry mtime check is a one-directional brake: removing it deletes the same set or more, not a retention policy. Fixture deletion policy = its own server PID exited; PID reuse only spares. Bounce holder check is a brake on signalling, not a decision to delete. No --apply was run by this seat.

magicWand: a shared bounded subprocess/output acquisition primitive, exercised against non-exiting helpers and EOF retention, so a new fallback cannot silently bypass a previously bounded stop path.
difficulties: current cost prose says lsof~0.1s and10s cap without retained timing/end-to-end proof; record estimates as estimates and configured waits as configured waits. Feedback retained in this governed output rather than editing the read-only product tree.

Evidence ledger /tmp/performance-298-static-cost.json. Handover: repair P298-001 in the coder worktree, provide exact final head and retained bounded-helper smoke/test receipt for round2; keep final review at most two rounds. Any genuinely new final-round issue goes to pm-001 under C34 rather than starting a third round. Retain performance/298 even after this BLOCK.
